title: Bilinear comparison descent through rationalization and common coefficient fields
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and an algebraic closure $\Omega/\mathbf Q_\ell$. Index by finite intermediate extensions $\mathbf Q_\ell\subseteq E\subset\Omega$, with valuation ring $R_E=\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. For each $E$ let $\mathcal C_E,\mathcal D_E$ be $R_E$-linear categories [def-weil-linear-category]. Suppose they have scalar-extension functors $S^C_{L/E},S^D_{L/E}$, linear through $R_E\to R_L$, with specified identity and tower natural isomorphisms satisfying the unit and associativity cocycles. Let $U_E,V_E:\mathcal C_E\times\mathcal C_E\to\mathcal D_E$ be separately $R_E$-linear bifunctors. Supply natural isomorphisms
$$\lambda^U_{L/E}:S^D_{L/E}U_E\cong U_L(S^C_{L/E},S^C_{L/E}),\qquad\lambda^V_{L/E}:S^D_{L/E}V_E\cong V_L(S^C_{L/E},S^C_{L/E})$$
obeying the identity and tower cocycles. Suppose natural isomorphisms $\eta_E:U_E\cong V_E$ satisfy
$$\lambda^V_{L/E}\,S^D_{L/E}(\eta_E)=\eta_L\,\lambda^U_{L/E}.$$

Use raw rationalizations with the same objects and Hom modules tensored over $R_E$ with $E$ [def-weil-linear-scalar-localization]. There are unique separately $E$-linear extensions of $U_E,V_E$ with morphism action
$$\overline U_E(u\otimes a,v\otimes b)=U_E(u,v)\otimes ab$$
and the analogous formula for $V_E$, extended additively. The components $\eta_E\otimes1$, with inverses $\eta_E^{-1}\otimes1$, are a natural isomorphism on these rationalizations, and the scalar square above remains an equality. No Hom module is required to be torsion-free.

For either family $\mathcal A=\mathcal C,\mathcal D$, define the common-stage category to have objects $(E,A)$ and Hom groups
$$\operatorname{Hom}((E,A),(E',A'))=\varinjlim_{L\supset E,E'}\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A_L[1/\varpi_L]}(S^A_{L/E}A,S^A_{L/E'}A'),$$
with composition at a common stage and equality after passage to a further stage, as in [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. The extensions of $U,V$ induce bifunctors on these common-stage categories: on objects their coefficient field is $K=E_1E_2$, and on arrows they use the given $\lambda$ to identify the source and target at a common field. They carry a natural isomorphism with the following specified representative. For inputs $(E_1,A),(E_2,B)$ put $A_K=S^C_{K/E_1}A$, $B_K=S^C_{K/E_2}B$. At every $L\supset K$, its representative from $S^D_{L/K}\overline U_K(A_K,B_K)$ to $S^D_{L/K}\overline V_K(A_K,B_K)$ is
$$ (\overline\lambda^V_{L/K})^{-1}\,\overline\eta_{L;S^C_{L/K}A_K,S^C_{L/K}B_K}\,\overline\lambda^U_{L/K}.$$
Its inverse is the analogous conjugate of $\overline\eta_L^{-1}$. These classes are independent of the field and of arrow representatives; different initial common fields are compared at a further common extension. These constructions preserve identities, vertical composition, and whiskering in each variable by scalar-compatible linear functors or separately linear bifunctors. Thus every finite well-typed equation between such composites descends, including supplied associativity, signed symmetry, action-unit, pullback-composition and scalar-extension equations. No idempotent completion is included.

proof.text: Factor each integral bifunctor arrow map into its two slots to obtain integralHom, using separate linearity and bilinear composition. Apply TensorProduct.lift and LinearMap.baseChange to that bilinear map, then AlgebraTensorModule.distribBaseChange.symm and TensorProduct.curry. The resulting explicit rawHom has the product-of-scalars pure-tensor formula. Tensor induction proves composition and uniqueness without Hom injectivity. Store the bilinear map as rawHomLinear; rawHom evaluates its two toFun projections directly. Its proved zero, addition, scalar and pure-tensor formulas give the same bilinearity API with fewer elaborator coercion searches.

proof.text: Use the actual ScalarLocalization category [def-weil-linear-scalar-localization]. Tensor induction in the four input arrows reduces preservation of composition to the pure-tensor composition formula and U.map_comp. Identities follow from U.map_id. Tensor induction together with separate linearity proves uniqueness of the functor with the prescribed object and pure-tensor action. Its composition is the uniquely determined bilinear extension proved in [lem-weil-linear-scalar-localization-category], which remains a transitive dependency. The private tensorComp function evaluates the existing curried composition map directly; its proved zero, addition and pure-tensor laws preserve exactly that composition while avoiding repeated coercion synthesis. The helper simp rules are local.

proof.text: Put $\bar\eta_{A,B}=\eta_{A,B}\otimes1$. For $f\otimes a:A\to A'$ and $g\otimes b:B\to B'$, its naturality square is precisely the integral equality $V_E(f,g)\eta_{A,B}=\eta_{A',B'}U_E(f,g)$ tensored with $ab$. Additivity in each input extends this to all arrows. The two inverse equations are $(\eta^{-1}\eta)\otimes1=1\otimes1$ and $(\eta\eta^{-1})\otimes1=1\otimes1$. Thus these are actual natural isomorphisms even when localization kills nonzero integral morphisms.

source.place: Raw Hom localization; naturality and inverse equations on pure tensors

proof.text: Construct the integer-ring inclusion as the field inclusion restricted to the recorded valuation subrings [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. The larger spectral absolute value restricts to the smaller one by uniqueness [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-absolute-value]; the DVR membership characterization [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr] then proves preservation of integers. This is the same restriction map as integralScalarIntegerInclusion, without importing its geometric scalar-extension development. Extend each transition functor semilinearly by [lem-pur-semilinear-scalar-localization], taking $R=R_E$, $S=R_L$, $t=\varpi_E$, $u=\varpi_L$. The image of $t$ is nonzero, hence invertible in $L$; $R_E[1/t]=E$ and $R_L[1/u]=L$ by [lem-weil-l-adic-integers-localization-uniformizer]. The cited semilinear lemma extends their unit and tower isomorphisms with their equations. For a scalar comparison $\lambda^U$, naturality on $f\otimes a,g\otimes b$ follows by multiplying its integral naturality equality by the image of $ab$ in $L$; extend by sums. Its inverse is localized in the same way. The identity and tower equations for $\lambda^U,\lambda^V$, and the square $\lambda^V S^D(\eta)=\eta\lambda^U$, are equalities of components; tensor each equality with $1$. We henceforth omit bars on the rationalized functors and comparisons.

proof.text: Finite intermediate extensions have their finite compositum as upper bound by [def-weil-finite-subextension-directed-set]. For the abstract directed preorder use the already proved StageSystem.PairCategory calculus in WeilConjectures.CategoryTheory.StageSystem.Basic: exists_mkHom_eq gives representatives, mkHom_tr transports them, and mkHom_eq_mkHom_iff gives eventual equality. These facts apply directly to the common-stage quotient used in the statements.

proof.text: Use the adopted StageSystem quotient calculus. Form the product stage system and its two projection morphisms. Its pair-category diagonal into the product of pair categories is fully faithful: represent two arrows at common upper stages for surjectivity, and combine their eventual-equality stages for injectivity. Choose at join(i,j) the two transported objects; full faithfulness lifts conjugation by isoToStage to a functor pairing. Compose pairing with the stage-system morphism furnished by the bilinear family. Its arrow formula is exactly endpoint-conjugated U_L(f,g), by mapAt and the two associators. The quotient calculus proves all representative and category laws.

proof.text:
Let $x=((E,A),(F,B))$, $K=EF$, and $W_x=U_K(S^C_{K/E}A,S^C_{K/F}B)$. For $L\supset K$ define the endpoint identification
$$d^U_{L,x}=U_L(a^C_{L,K,E,A},a^C_{L,K,F,B})\lambda^U_{L/K;S^C_{K/E}A,S^C_{K/F}B}:S^D_{L/K}W_x\xrightarrow{\sim}U_L(S^C_{L/E}A,S^C_{L/F}B).$$
Define $d^V$ by replacing $U$ with $V$. Given $x'$ with output field $K'$ and input arrows represented by $f,g$ over $L\supset K,K'$, prescribe the image arrow to be
$$(d^U_{L,x'})^{-1}U_L(f,g)d^U_{L,x}.$$
Such an $L$ exists by [def-weil-finite-subextension-directed-set]. These formulas give the claimed compositum object map and completely typed arrow representatives.

proof.text: For the resulting functor, pairing_map follows by applying the faithful diagonal and the common-stage isoToStage formulas. The family stage-system morphism sends this representative by mapAt, giving endpoint U_L(f,g) endpoint inverse. StageSystem.tr_tr, mkHom_comp_mkHom and the eventual equality criterion already imply the required tower and transport independence. No separate direct-limit construction is required.

proof.text: If either input representative changes, the old and new representatives become equal at a common stage; for the two inputs take a further compositum of their equality stages. The transport equality in step 8 then makes the two output representatives equal. This is exactly the StageSystem.PairCategory.mkHom_eq_mkHom_iff equality criterion; no transition map has to be injective. On identity arrows the output formula is $d^{-1}1d=1$. For composable pairs represented together, its composite is $d_{x''}^{-1}U(f',g')d_{x'}d_{x'}^{-1}U(f,g)d_x=d_{x''}^{-1}U(f'f,g'g)d_x$. These calculations prove functoriality of both descended bifunctors.

proof.text:
For $x$ as above let $e_x=\eta_{K;S^C_{K/E}A,S^C_{K/F}B}$. The scalar square at $K\subset L$ says
$$S^D_{L/K}(e_x)=(\lambda^V_{L/K})^{-1}\eta_{L;S^C_{L/K}S^C_{K/E}A,S^C_{L/K}S^C_{K/F}B}\lambda^U_{L/K}.$$
This is exactly the representative requested in the statement. Naturality of $\eta_L$ with the two $a^C$ components further identifies it with
$$(d^V_{L,x})^{-1}\eta_{L;S^C_{L/E}A,S^C_{L/F}B}d^U_{L,x}.$$
The class can be defined using $L=K$, with the unit comparisons; all larger $L$ represent that same class because their formulas are $S^D_{L/K}(e_x)$. Replacing $\eta$ by its inverse gives its inverse class; their products are identities. No assertion of literal equality of differently typed endpoints is made.

source.place: Common-stage Hom formula; agent verification for the abstract linear categories of this statement

proof.text:
For an input pair arrow $(f,g)$ represented at $L$, multiply its $V$-image by the component of step 10. Cancelling the adjacent $d^V_{L,x}(d^V_{L,x})^{-1}$ gives
$$(d^V_{L,x'})^{-1}V_L(f,g)\eta_{L,x_L}d^U_{L,x}=(d^V_{L,x'})^{-1}\eta_{L,x'_L}U_L(f,g)d^U_{L,x},$$
by the rational naturality proved in step 3. Insert $d^U_{L,x'}(d^U_{L,x'})^{-1}$ to obtain the other naturality composite. Step 8 and the existing StageSystem eventual-equality criterion show this same equation is independent of arrow representatives. If a different initial common field $K_1$ is used for the output object, compare at $M\supset K,K_1$. The canonical comparison from the $K$-output to the $K_1$-output is represented by $(d^U_{M,x,K_1})^{-1}d^U_{M,x,K}$, and similarly for $V$. Step 8 makes these independent of $M$. Multiplying them through the component formula cancels $d$ and proves that the two components agree under these comparisons. Their identities, inverses and cocycles also follow by cancelling the middle $d d^{-1}$.

proof.text: For localized transformations identities and vertical composition are preserved because $(\theta\eta)\otimes1=(\theta\otimes1)(\eta\otimes1)$. For whiskering by a linear functor, or in either slot of a separately linear bifunctor, step 1 gives the same identity by setting all unchanged scalar factors to $1$; thus applying a functor to a transformation component commutes with extension. For common-stage components write each transformation in the form $d_{\mathrm{out}}^{-1}\eta_Ld_{\mathrm{in}}$ from step 10. Vertical composition cancels the intermediate $d_{\mathrm{in}}d_{\mathrm{in}}^{-1}$. Whiskering gives the same formula: apply the stage functor (in the specified slot) to the three factors and compose its scalar comparison with those of that slot. Its comparison naturality moves that scalar comparison across $\eta_L$, leaving just the outside identifications. In an output slot this is an equality: for $F$ with comparison $\mu$, $F_L(d_{\mathrm{out}})\mu$ and $F_L(d_{\mathrm{in}})\mu$ are the $d$'s of $FU,FV$ for $\lambda^{FU}=F_L(\lambda^U)\mu$. In an input slot the two objects differ: $U$ of the descended $F(E,A)=(E,F_EA)$ has $K$-object $U_K(S_{K/E}F_EA,B_K)$, the family $U(F-,-)$ has $U_K(F_KS_{K/E}A,B_K)$. Identify them by the class represented at $L$ by $(d^{U(F,1)}_{L,x})^{-1}U_L(\mu_{L/E,A},1)d^U_{L,x_F}$. It is independent of $L$ by step 8 and the tower equation for $\mu$. Since $F$ sends $f$ to $\mu^{-1}F_L(f)\mu$, it is natural, and the whiskered components agree after conjugation by it. This also covers nested bifunctors, using the supplied tower equations to identify their chosen common fields.

proof.text: Apply StageSystem.PairCategory.mkHom_eq_mkHom_iff to the two supplied representatives at L: equality of their images after a common further stage gives equality of the two quotient classes. After vertical composition or whiskering the previous component formulas give the specified representatives, so the same criterion applies to every finite well-typed equation. The finite compositum upper bound is supplied by [def-weil-finite-subextension-directed-set].
